Total households in Mikusa domain: 1,976. The leading 千 carries the slanted stroke on top (not a plain 十 cross), so the magnitude is thousands — 1,976, not 1,990. The neighbouring Mineoka domain (p. 131) is recorded with the identical household count, 千九百七十六戸; each figure is printed in its own domain's block, so the duplication sits in the source.

Total population as printed: 8,961 — about 4.5 persons per household across 1,976 households. FLAG: the male/female split below sums to only 8,832 (男4,518 + 女4,314), leaving the printed total 129 short. This cannot be a misreading of the split: both sub-counts take the form [digit]千[digit]百十[digit], so their units digits (8 and 4) must produce a total ending in 2, never in 1. The same total, 八千九百六十一人, is printed for the next domain, Miike, on p. 135, where it reconciles exactly (4,508 + 4,453); and Mikusa's household count likewise duplicates that of the preceding domain, Mineoka (p. 131). Mikusa's entry therefore sits between two duplicated figures — a transmission error in the source rather than a reading error — though which entry was copied from which is not established. Transcribed and parsed as printed.

外ニ　高十石　元朱印地
外（ほか）に、高 十石、元朱印地（もとしゅいんち）

In addition: 10 koku, formerly vermilion-seal (shuinchi) land — a shogunal grant standing outside the domain's assessed kokudaka. 外ニ prints as a small right-offset superscript label, with 元朱印地 in smaller type beneath the value. This is Mikusa's, not Miike's: it stands to the RIGHT of the ○三池藩 marker, and the warichu note below names the holder as a temple in Harima — Mikusa's province. Miike's lands lay elsewhere entirely: p. 134 breaks its tax down by 筑後國三池五ヶ村 (Chikugo) and 岩代國伊達郡六ヶ村 (Iwashiro).
外
播磨加玉郡奥山村　奥山寺
播磨（はりま）加東郡（かとうぐん）奥山村、奥山寺（おくやまでら）

Warichu (two-column inset note) plus a widely spaced temple name, identifying the holder of the 10 koku of former vermilion-seal land above: Okuyama-dera, Okuyama village, Harima province. Read right column top-to-bottom, then left: 播磨加玉 / 郡奥山村. The district glyph is genuinely printed 玉, giving 'Katama district' — but no such district existed in Harima. The glyph is unambiguous at high magnification: three horizontals, a single centre vertical, and a dot in the lower-right quadrant; 東 would require a 日 box (two further verticals), and the space beside the centre stroke is clean white. This is almost certainly 加東郡 (Katō) — the Harima district where Mikusa domain sat — most likely a typesetter's misreading of a cursive 東 in the manuscript. Transcribed verbatim as printed.

○三池藩（みいけはん）

Maru-marker opening the Miike domain block — the only marker on this page. It sets the ownership boundary: everything printed to its right belongs to the previous domain, Mikusa (whose ○三草藩 marker stands on the facing page), and everything to its left is Miike's. Miike, a small Tachibana domain, held split territory in Chikugo and Iwashiro.
○三池藩
草高　壹萬千九百九十七石三斗八升五合七勺四才
草高（くさだか）一万千九百九十七石三斗八升五合七勺四才

Miike's kusadaka (gross assessed yield): 11,997.38574 koku — the first field of the Miike block, printed immediately left of the maru-marker. Sub-units run strictly descending (石 > 斗 > 升 > 合 > 勺 > 才), confirming the parse. The tens digit is 九, not 七: at high magnification it is stroke-for-stroke the same glyph as the 九 of 九百 two positions earlier in this same column and type size, and quite unlike the 七 in the units place just below it.
